assignmentHtml.task:
研究 CDC 管道中的 Kafka 恰好一次语义和 Debezium 细节。调查：

  1. Kafka 生产者幂等性与事务（KIP-98）、消费者组提交，以及 broker 故障时会发生什么。
  2. Debezium 连接器重启行为——偏移量、模式注册中心、连接器状态。
  3. Kafka Connect 分布式模式——偏移量存储、连接器重启、模式演进处理。
  4. 完整链路（源 → Kafka → 接收端）中恰好一次、至少一次和至多一次投递保证的比较。
  5. Kafka 消费者停机时，“重放”意味着什么——能否从旧偏移量重新读取？对保留策略的依赖。
  6. 墓碑消息与日志压缩。
    如有相关性，请以具体 Kafka 版本为依据。
assignmentHtml.context: 证据截止日期为 2026-09-16。工作负载 B 要求从 PostgreSQL 进行 CDC，涉及删除、乱序投递、连接器重启、模式变更和回填。工作负载 F 要求调查重放、偏移量、检查点、幂等性、对保留策略的依赖，以及回滚语义。需要理解保证来自哪里，以及在哪里失效。
assignmentHtml.expected_output: 提供 Kafka + Debezium 的详细调研，涵盖恰好一次、重放、偏移量、幂等性、保留策略、连接器重启，并附来源 URL。

answerHtml:
COMPREHENSIVE INVESTIGATION: Kafka + Debezium CDC Pipeline — Exactly-Once, Replay, Offsets, Idempotence, Retention, Connector Restarts

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  1. KAFKA PRODUCER IDEMPOTENCE & TRANSACTIONS (KIP-98), CONSUMER GROUP COMMITS, BROKER FAILURE
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Idempotence (KIP-129 / KIP-679):

  • Since Kafka 3.0, enable.idempotence=true and acks=all are the DEFAULT producer settings (KIP-679) [4].
  • Each producer instance gets a unique Producer ID (PID). Every batch gets a sequence number per partition; the broker dedupes based on persisted sequence state (written to a .snapshot file) [1][2].
  • Guarantees exactly-once-per-partition within a single producer session. Does NOT protect across producer restarts unless transactional.id is used [2].
  • OutOfOrderSequenceException and ProducerFencedException are unrecoverable — the app must close and create a new producer [2].

Transactions (KIP-98):

  • Requires a unique transactional.id per logical producer. On initTransactions(), the transaction coordinator (a broker component managing the internal __transaction_state topic) recovers any in-flight transactions for that ID, allocates the same PID with an incremented epoch, and fences older zombie instances of the same transactional.id with ProducerFencedException [2][3].
  • Two-phase commit: transaction states are Undecided → PrepareCommit/PrepareAbort → CompleteCommit/CompleteAbort. Control records (commit/abort markers) are appended to user partitions [2].
  • LSO (Last Stable Offset) = highest offset where all lower offsets are decided; HW ≤ LEO; LSO ≤ HW ≤ LEO. Consumers with isolation.level=read_committed only read up to LSO and filter out aborted transactions [2][5].
  • End-to-end EOS requires the consumer to use read_committed [1][3].

Consumer Group Commits:

  • Offsets committed to the internal __consumer_offsets topic (compacted, retention controlled by offsets.retention.minutes, default 7 days) [8].
  • A crash between processing and committing means re-processing from the last committed offset.

Broker Failure:

  • The controller elects new leaders from the ISR. With acks=all, a message is committed only when all in-sync replicas have applied it, so no data is lost when a leader fails [6].
  • By default (unclean.leader.election.enable=false), Kafka waits for an ISR replica to recover, favoring consistency over availability [6].
  • Unclean leader election risks losing committed messages but keeps the partition available [6].
  • Uncommitted (in-flight) data from a failed leader may be lost if the ISR shrinks below min.insync.replicas before the producer gets an ack [6].

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
2. DEBEZIUM CONNECTOR RESTART BEHAVIOR — OFFSETS, SCHEMA REGISTRY, CONNECTOR STATE
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Offsets (PostgreSQL example — LSN as offset):

  • Debezium records the WAL position (LSN) with each event. Kafka Connect flushes the offset to its offset store (Kafka topic in distributed mode; file in standalone) periodically — default offset.flush.interval.ms=60000 [9][10].
  • On restart, the connector requests PostgreSQL to resume streaming from the last recorded LSN, which is retained by the logical replication slot [11].
  • If Kafka Connect crashes, only the LAST FLUSHED offset is recovered — events published between the last flush and the crash are re-emitted (at-least-once) [10][11].
  • If the offset store is lost (topic deleted, compaction failure), the connector behaves per snapshot.mode: default initial triggers a full re-snapshot → duplicates downstream [11][12].
  • A dropped replication slot while offline makes the stored LSN invalid → fatal error requiring connector recreation + resnapshot [12].

Snapshot modes (critical for restart semantics) [11]:

  • initial (default): snapshot only if no offsets exist; otherwise stream from stored LSN.
  • always: full snapshot on every start — useful after cluster failover.
  • no_data: never snapshot; stream from replication slot creation point or stored LSN.
  • when_needed: snapshot if offsets missing OR stored LSN is no longer available on the server.
  • configuration_based / custom: advanced control.

Schema Registry:

  • Debezium generates record schemas dynamically from DB table structure. With Avro converters, each schema version is registered in Schema Registry (Confluent or Apicurio) with auto-registration [13].
  • A DB schema change (e.g., ADD COLUMN) produces a new Avro schema version. Whether this succeeds depends on the registry's compatibility mode [13][14].
  • BACKWARD compat (default): new schema can read old data. Adding an optional field is backward compatible; adding a REQUIRED field without a default is rejected → connector parks in retry loop, topic goes silent [14][15].
  • FULL_TRANSITIVE is recommended for CDC where producers and consumers upgrade independently [15].

Connector State:

  • Debezium maintains an internal schema history (in-memory by default; configurable to Kafka/File/JDBC/Redis/S3) recording DB DDL/structure changes [7].
  • This schema history is separate from external Schema Registry and is used to interpret change events during recovery [7].

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
3. KAFKA CONNECT DISTRIBUTED MODE — OFFSETS STORAGE, CONNECTOR RESTARTS, SCHEMA EVOLUTION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Offsets Storage:

  • Distributed mode stores offsets, configs, and task statuses in Kafka topics: offset.storage.topic (many partitions, replicated, compacted), config.storage.topic (single partition, compacted), status.storage.topic [16].
  • The framework commits offsets automatically at offset.flush.interval.ms intervals; REST API provides GET/PATCH/DELETE connector offsets (connector must be stopped) [16].
  • Offsets are compacted so only the latest offset per connector/task partition is retained [16].

Connector Restarts:

  • REST API: POST /connectors/{name}/restart?includeTasks=<true|false>&onlyFailed=<true|false>; POST /connectors/{name}/tasks/{taskId}/restart [16].
  • Default behavior is "fail fast" (errors.tolerance=none, errors.retry.timeout=0). Can be configured for retries and dead-letter queuing [16].
  • On worker restart, connectors recover from their last committed offsets in the offset storage topic [16].
  • Restarting a connector with a different name creates a NEW offset key → connector has no prior position → falls back to snapshot behavior [12].

Exactly-Once for Source Connectors (KIP-618, Kafka 3.3+):

  • Worker config: exactly.once.source.support=enabled. Connector config: exactly.once.support=required (or requested) and transaction.boundary=poll (default) [17][18].
  • The framework commits source offsets and produced records atomically in one Kafka transaction per poll batch [18][19].
  • Debezium PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Oracle, SQL Server support this [17].
  • CAVEAT: Jepsen reports (Redpanda, Bufstream) highlight open issues in Kafka's transaction protocol (KAFKA-17734, KAFKA-17754, KAFKA-17582) that may affect EOS correctness [17].
  • Snapshot phase is NOT covered by EOS: a mid-snapshot crash causes a full re-snapshot and duplicates [17][18].

Schema Evolution Handling:

  • Kafka Connect does not auto-manage schemas; the SetSchemaMetadata transform can set schema name/version explicitly [16].
  • Schema evolution is managed externally via Schema Registry with compatibility modes (BACKWARD/FORWARD/FULL/TRANSITIVE) [14].

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
4. EXACTLY-ONCE VS AT-LEAST-ONCE VS AT-MOST-ONCE THROUGH THE FULL CHAIN
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Source → Kafka (Debezium):

  • Default: AT-LEAST-ONCE. Debezium commits offset AFTER writing events; crash in between → re-emission [10][17].
  • With Kafka Connect EOS (KIP-618, Kafka 3.3+, exactly.once.support=required): effectively exactly-once for the STREAMING phase [17][18].
  • Snapshot phase remains at-least-once regardless [17][18].
  • Consumer-side: must use isolation.level=read_committed to see only committed records [1][2].

Kafka Transport:

  • Producer: idempotence (per-partition EOS, default since 3.0) + transactions (cross-partition atomicity) [1][2].
  • Broker: replication with acks=all guarantees no loss of committed data across broker failures [6].

Kafka → Sink:

  • Sink connectors: EOS requires idempotent sink writes + atomic offset/data storage (e.g., HDFS connector historically) [20]. Most sinks are at-least-once.
  • Two-phase-commit sinks can achieve EOS [20].

End-to-End Analysis (where guarantees BREAK) [10][15][17]:

  • The offset-commit gap: events published but not yet flushed to the offset store are replayed on crash — the primary duplicate source [10][15].
  • Multi-destination fan-out: cannot atomically commit to two different downstream systems [10].
  • Snapshot/restart transitions: wrong snapshot.mode causes either full re-snapshots (duplicates) or missed data (slot lost) [12][15].
  • Schema changes: a DDL change can park the connector in a retry loop (registry rejection) — topic goes silent, no errors [15].
  • Cross-connector consistency: independent offset stores mean JOINs across tables are not globally consistent [10].
  • True end-to-end EOS requires: idempotent sink keyed on (PK + log position), alerting on silence, and rehearsed restart procedures [15].

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
5. REPLAY FOR A KAFKA CONSUMER OUTAGE — OLD OFFSETS, RETENTION DEPENDENCIES
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

What 'replay' means:

  • A consumer outage doesn't delete data (assuming retention). On return, the consumer resumes from its last committed offset in __consumer_offsets [8].
  • To RE-READ from an old offset: use auto.offset.reset=earliest with a NEW consumer group, or manually reset offsets via the kafka-consumer-groups.sh --reset-offsets tool or the Connect REST PATCH offsets API [8][16].
  • Consumers can seek to any offset that still exists in the log, provided the data hasn't been purged [8].

Retention Dependencies (critical) [8]:

  • Log retention (retention.ms/retention.bytes) determines how long data is available for replay. If a consumer is down longer than retention, data is permanently gone — even earliest cannot recover it [8].
  • Committed offsets have SEPARATE retention: offsets.retention.minutes (default 10080 = 7 days). After this period, offsets are deleted and a consumer group resets to auto.offset.reset behavior [8].
  • For CDC pipelines: align log retention with expected consumer downtime. Short retention (e.g., 24h) with a week-long outage = data loss [8].
  • Compacted topics: only the LATEST value per key is guaranteed retained; intermediate versions may be compacted away. Consumers lagging > delete.retention.ms (default 24h) may miss tombstones [4].

Replay with Debezium:

  • To replay Kafka topic data, you'd create a new consumer group (or reset offsets) and reprocess from an old offset. Downstream must be idempotent to absorb duplicates [8].
  • Debezium itself cannot replay database history from Kafka unless the Kafka topic retains the data (retention) and the sink supports idempotent upserts.

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
6. TOMBSTONE MESSAGES AND LOG COMPACTION
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

Log Compaction Mechanics [4]:

  • Compaction retains the latest value per message KEY, discarding older versions. It operates on the log TAIL; the head remains dense with sequential offsets [4].
  • Compacted records keep their original offsets — offsets remain valid positions even if the record was compacted away [4].
  • Guarantees: (1) caught-up consumers see every written message; (2) ordering preserved; (3) offsets never change; (4) consumers starting from offset 0 see at least the final state of all records + all delete markers IF they reach the head within delete.retention.ms [4].
  • min.compaction.lag.ms: minimum time before a record is eligible for compaction. max.compaction.lag.ms: maximum delay [4].

Tombstones [4]:

  • A message with a key and null VALUE is a delete marker (tombstone). Compaction removes all previous records with that key upon seeing the tombstone [4].
  • Tombstones themselves are removed after delete.retention.ms (default 24 hours) to free space [4].
  • Slow consumers (lagging > delete.retention.ms) may MISS the tombstone → they reintroduce deleted data on replay. This is why delete.retention.ms bounds the time for a full 0-offset scan [4].

Debezium + Tombstones (CDC deletes) [11]:

  • The PostgreSQL connector emits a DELETE event followed by a tombstone (null value) with the same key when tombstones.on.delete=true (default). This enables Kafka to fully remove the row's history from a compacted topic [11].
  • tombstones.on.delete=false emits only the DELETE event (no tombstone) — compaction leaves the last known value [11].
  • REPLICA IDENTITY setting (FULL/INDEX/DEFAULT/NOTHING) controls what 'before' data is captured for UPDATE/DELETE events [11].
  • Primary key updates emit a DELETE for the old key + CREATE for the new key [11].

Compaction Caveats [4]:

  • Compaction timing is non-deterministic; multiple records with the same key can coexist transiently [4].
  • Compacted topics REQUIRE keyed records. Compaction does not guarantee only one record per key at all times [4].
  • Compaction runs only when partition conditions are met (dirty ratio, inactive segments) [4].

═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
VERSION ANCHORS
═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

  • Kafka 0.11: KIP-98 transactions introduced [1][2]
  • Kafka 3.0: KIP-679 — idempotence + acks=all become defaults [2][21]
  • Kafka 3.3: KIP-618 — exactly-once support for source connectors in Kafka Connect [17][18]
  • Debezium: EOS supported for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Oracle, SQL Server with Kafka Connect 3.3+ [17]
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    KEY TAKEAWAY FOR WORKLOADS B & F
    ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    For CDC from PostgreSQL with deletes, out-of-order delivery, connector restarts, schema changes, and backfills:
  1. Debezium is at-least-once by default into Kafka; EOS requires Kafka 3.3+ with explicit config and still excludes the snapshot phase.
  2. Replication slots retain WAL indefinitely during outages — monitor disk (set max_slot_wal_keep_size) [11][15].
  3. Offsets flush on interval — design sinks as idempotent upserts keyed on (PK + LSN) [15].
  4. Schema Registry compatibility must be negotiated (FULL_TRANSITIVE recommended); DDL changes can silently stop the pipeline [15].
  5. Replay depends entirely on Kafka log retention vs. consumer downtime; tombstone visibility depends on delete.retention.ms vs. consumer lag [4][8].
  6. Config changes (connector name, snapshot.mode) are deployments with restart semantics — drill them before production [15].

evidence.snippet: Comprehensive overview of idempotence (sequence numbers per partition), transactions (KIP-98), isolation levels (read_committed/read_uncommitted), and the cooperation required between producer/consumer/broker for end-to-end EOS. Notes Kafka tolerates n-1 broker failures via replication.
evidence.supports: Kafka EOS foundations: idempotence per-partition, transactions across partitions, consumer isolation levels, broker failure handling

evidence.snippet: Since Kafka 3.0, idempotence is enabled by default (acks=all, enable.idempotence=true per KIP-679). Transactional.id identifies logical producer across restarts; PID+epoch enable zombie fencing. __transaction_state topic holds coordinator state. LSO/HW/LEO definitions given. ProducerFencedException requires new producer instance.
evidence.supports: Idempotence default since 3.0; transactional.id/fencing mechanics; LSO concept; unrecoverable exceptions

evidence.snippet: transactional.id enables zombie fencing via epoch increments. Two-phase commit with transaction markers written to user partitions. Consumer reads only committed messages with read_committed. Atomic write of output + input offset commit enables end-to-end EOS.
evidence.supports: Zombie fencing, two-phase commit, atomic offset+output commits for EOS

evidence.snippet: ISR model: committed = all in-sync replicas applied. acks=all waits for full ISR set. Controller elects leaders from ISR on failure. Default unclean.leader.election.enable=false favors consistency. f+1 replicas tolerate f failures. min.insync.replicas controls durability threshold.
evidence.supports: Broker failure handling, ISR-based durability, unclean leader election tradeoff

evidence.snippet: Compaction retains latest value per key; tombstones (key + null value) enable deletes; tombstones removed after delete.retention.ms (default 24h). Guarantees: caught-up consumers see all messages, ordering preserved, offsets immutable, consumers from offset 0 see final state plus delete markers if reaching head within delete.retention.ms. min/max.compaction.lag.ms control timing.
evidence.supports: Log compaction mechanics, tombstone semantics, delete.retention.ms dependency for slow consumers

evidence.snippet: Debezium requires persistent storage for offsets and internal schema history. Options: Kafka (distributed), File (standalone), Memory (volatile), JDBC, Redis, S3, Azure Blob, RocketMQ. Kafka offset store topic must be compacted.
evidence.supports: Debezium state storage options, Kafka-backed offset/schema-history topics in distributed mode

evidence.snippet: LSN offsets recorded per event; connector resumes from last recorded LSN via replication slot. snapshot.mode options (initial/always/no_data/when_needed/configuration_based/custom). Deletes followed by tombstone (tombstones.on.delete=true default). REPLICA IDENTITY controls before-data. No DDL capture. PK changes emit DELETE+CREATE.
evidence.supports: PostgreSQL connector restart behavior, LSN offsets, snapshot modes, tombstone emission, replication slot dependency

evidence.snippet: Debezium provides at-least-once by default. Kafka Connect EOS (KIP-618) available for PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, MongoDB, Oracle, SQL Server. Requires Kafka distributed mode, Connect 3.3+, worker config exactly.once.source.support=enabled, connector config exactly.once.support=required, transaction.boundary=poll. Docs caution about open Kafka issues (KAFKA-17734, KAFKA-17754, KAFKA-17582) from Jepsen reports.
evidence.supports: Which Debezium connectors support EOS, required configuration, documented caveats about unproven correctness

evidence.snippet: Debezium aimed only at at-least-once. KIP-618 in Kafka 3.3.0 enabled EOS for source connectors. Events written in uncommitted transactions invisible to consumers until offset commit. Snapshot phase failure requires full re-snapshot → duplicates. Streaming phase works out-of-the-box with poll boundary. Recommended testing with exactly.once.support=requested.
evidence.supports: Debezium EOS path, snapshot-phase limitation, poll-boundary alignment

evidence.snippet: Distributed mode stores offsets/configs/statuses in Kafka topics (offset.storage.topic many partitions + replicated + compacted; config.storage.topic single partition). REST API: POST /connectors/{name}/restart (includeTasks, onlyFailed params), POST /connectors/{name}/tasks/{taskId}/restart. Offsets: GET/PATCH/DELETE /connectors/{name}/offsets (connector must be stopped). Default fail-fast error behavior; errors.tolerance and errors.retry.timeout configurable.
evidence.supports: Kafka Connect distributed mode offsets storage, connector restart APIs, offset management endpoints

evidence.snippet: KIP-618: source connectors provide meaningful offsets per record and resume exactly. Framework commits transaction per poll() batch by default; transaction.boundary=connector allows custom boundaries. exactlyOnceSupport() validates EOS capability. Framework commits offsets atomically with transaction commit.
evidence.supports: KIP-618 mechanics: how framework coordinates offset commits with transactions for source connectors

evidence.snippet: auto.offset.reset: earliest (from beginning), latest (new messages only), none (error). Committed offsets live in __consumer_offsets topic with retention offsets.retention.minutes (default 7 days). If log retention shorter than consumer lag, even earliest cannot recover purged messages. Data loss occurs when offsets expire and data is gone; duplication occurs with earliest reset.
evidence.supports: Consumer group replay semantics, offset retention vs. log retention dependency, reset behaviors

evidence.snippet: Debezium offsets = internal bookmarks (LSN for Postgres, binlog file+pos for MySQL). Lost offsets + snapshot.mode=initial → full re-snapshot → duplicates. Renamed connector = new offset key = no prior position. Dropped replication slot → fatal error. MySQL binlog rotation → invalid offset. Recovery: update LSN manually in offset store or delete offset + re-snapshot. Offset topic should have replication.factor=3.
evidence.supports: Debezium offset failure scenarios, recovery paths, production protections

evidence.snippet: Debezium commits offset after writing events; crash between publish and flush → replay (at-least-once). offset.flush.interval.ms=60000 default. Snapshot phase has no transaction semantics → crash → full re-snapshot. Multi-destination fan-out cannot be atomic. Downstream must implement read-process-commit with idempotent writes for effectively-once. Debezium offsets not cross-connector consistent for JOINs.
evidence.supports: Where end-to-end EOS breaks in CDC: offset-commit gap, snapshot phase, multi-destination, schema changes

evidence.snippet: Production CDC breaks at seams: (1) offset flush interval → crash replays published events; defense = idempotent sink keyed on (PK + LSN). (2) Four restart scenarios: clean stop/resumes, crash/replays, config change/resets offsets, slot lost/requires backfill. (3) Schema Registry rejects incompatible DDL → connector parks in retry loop → topic silent. Defense: alert on absence, FULL_TRANSITIVE compatibility, DDL through contract process. (4) Stopped connector fills primary disk via replication slot; set max_slot_wal_keep_size.
evidence.supports: Practical failure modes in production CDC: restart semantics, snapshot/stream boundary, schema registry stalls, WAL retention

evidence.snippet: Avro serialization essential for Debezium because record schemas dynamically match DB table structures; schema evolution mechanism allows evolving schemas. Supports Confluent Schema Registry and Apicurio Registry with auto-registration. Apicurio Confluent compatibility mode for wire-format interoperability.
evidence.supports: Debezium + Schema Registry integration, dynamic schema generation, evolution mechanism

evidence.snippet: Compatibility modes: BACKWARD (default, consumers with new schema read old data), FORWARD, FULL (both directions), NONE, plus transitive variants. For Avro: adding/removing optional fields fully compatible; adding required fields only forward-compatible. Mode dictates upgrade order: BACKWARD → upgrade consumers first; FORWARD → upgrade producers first; FULL → independent.
evidence.supports: Schema Registry compatibility modes, allowed changes by type, implications for CDC schema evolution

evidence.snippet: KIP-679: producer has stronger delivery guarantees by default starting Kafka 3.0 — idempotence enabled and acks set to all instead of 1.
evidence.supports: Version anchor: idempotence+acks=all defaults changed in Kafka 3.0
